source.title: EG-ARSA: An Expert-Grounded Open Model for Visual Road Safety Auditing in Low-Resource Settings
source.citation: Md Thamed Bin Zaman Chowdhury et al., 2026
source.authors: Md Thamed Bin Zaman Chowdhury; Moazzem Hossain

page_placements.theme: Student-over-supervisor gains from input asymmetry (privileged or degraded views), and bias from supervisor-assisted reference labels

record.tranche_reason: The study reports whether a student fine-tuned using teacher-generated supervision outperforms its teacher, addressing the weak-to-strong question in a visual road-auditing task with different models, supervision, and measures from the original.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a zero-shot versus fine-tuned student comparison and student-versus-teacher results, which are recorded below. It does not calculate PGR or isolate teacher-generated labels from the expert-gold and expert-silver supervision also used for training. Results cited from other work and the taxonomy-classifier agreement are not results on the claimed student-versus-supervisor effect.
record.test_reason: This is not a weak-to-strong test. The supervisor (gemma-4-31b-it, given an expert-calibrated, multi-image plus satellite prompt) is larger and better informed than the 8B student, so this is ordinary distillation from a stronger teacher. The student also trains directly on human expert-gold and expert-silver labels from the same tiers it is later scored on. The 'teacher' it beats is the 31B model run with the stripped single-image student prompt, not the supervisor as it actually produced labels. No PGR is computed, no strong ceiling is trained on true labels, and the effect of teacher labels is never isolated. The paper only calls its result 'a real-domain demonstration of weak-to-strong generalization' in related work and discussion.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that expert-grounded distillation into an 8B LoRA student beats the zero-shot base (+0.40 QWK) and outperforms both the leakage-free 31B teacher and Gemini-2.5-Flash. They attribute this to internalised grounding rather than scale. They also frame the student-beats-teacher result as a real-domain instance of weak-to-strong generalization, though their design does not match that setup.
record.recipe_differences: This is expert-grounded distillation for visual road auditing, not the original weak-to-strong recipe: a 31B teacher's prompted outputs supply the large street-view tier, but the student also trains on expert-gold and expert-silver records. The study evaluates risk accuracy, QWK, and blind expert scores rather than reporting PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different results across full-test and expert-grounded subsets, and between the raw risk operating point and an optional post-hoc offset; the headline student-versus-model comparison is on the expert-grounded subset.

fits_no_version.finding: An 8B VLM, LoRA-fine-tuned on 31B-teacher street-view audits plus human expert gold/silver records, beats the 31B teacher run with the stripped student prompt. Expert-subset risk accuracy is 0.737 vs 0.359 (Table 8); blind human risk-correct rate is 0.81 vs 0.42 (Table 9). The grounded teacher reached κ=0.74 with experts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Context distillation with mixed teacher and expert supervision lets a smaller student exceed its larger teacher when the teacher is evaluated without its labelling context.

record.problems: The student training data mix expert-produced labels with teacher-generated labels, preventing attribution of the result specifically to weak-label distillation. No PGR or strong model trained on true labels is reported. The teacher comparison removes its grounded prompt, while the student has internalised supervision produced using that prompt. The paper reports bootstrap intervals for many metrics, but not for all model comparisons.

untested.parts: There is no strong student trained on a weaker supervisor's labels, no PGR, no strong ceiling, and teacher labels are not isolated from expert labels.
Visual VLM setting, but no weak-to-strong setup is tested in it.

missing.what: Agreement of the grounded teacher (the actual supervising condition) with expert risk, κ=0.74. This is the relevant supervisor baseline and is not on the same metric as the student's accuracy. Section 5.7 also says QWK against the teacher reference is near zero on the gold and pooled expert subsets.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked every comparison row to V1/V6 and gave V1 supports and V6 supports. These are withdrawn. The supervisor is larger and has privileged inputs (multi-image plus satellite, corrective prompt). Expert labels from the evaluation tiers are in training. The 'teacher' baseline is a degraded version of the supervisor, so nothing here measures a strong student exceeding a weak supervisor.

versions.untested_parts: No PGR or strong model trained on true labels is reported. Training combines teacher-generated street-view annotations with expert-gold and expert-silver records; the contribution of each supervision source is not isolated.
No comparison of auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or loss variants by PGR.
No systematic variation of supervisor or student size, task, or representations, and no predictors of PGR.
No test of supervisor-uncheckable exploitation, distribution shift, or shared-error effects.
No theoretical result about conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
The tested setting is visual road auditing with vision-language models; no other non-language modality is tested.

relation.reason: Sections 2.2.1 and 6.1 invoke weak-to-strong generalization, but the experiment compares the student with a teacher deprived of its generation-time grounding rather than testing the catalog's claim.

tranche.reason: Expert-grounded distillation from a 31B teacher into an 8B student, supplemented by direct expert supervision, does not establish the weaker-supervisor/stronger-student setup required by the claim versions.

source_check.notes: The 262 entries are held-out expert-grounded test records, not the entire expert-grounded corpus. Teacher evaluation removes its generation-time grounding and additional images; gold and silver supervision uses expert records without a teacher model.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Fine-tuned visual road auditor versus the leakage-free teacher on expert-grounded entries
reader_labels.reason: The student has higher risk accuracy than the 31B teacher on the aggregate and both source subsets, and a higher blind-human risk-correct rate; see r3, r6, r9, and r12–r13.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: This study's expert-grounded distillation recipe and visual risk-auditing task
reader_labels.reason: The student is trained on a mixture that includes direct expert-gold and expert-silver supervision, so the results do not isolate fine-tuning on weaker-model labels or establish PGR; the full-test fine-tuning comparison is against a zero-shot base, not a weak supervisor (r1–r2).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Visual road-safety auditing with vision-language models
reader_labels.reason: In this visual task, the fine-tuned student improves over its zero-shot base and exceeds the leakage-free teacher on expert-grounded risk evaluation (r1–r3, r6, r9, r12).
